discovery: Quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution, founding quantum communication

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the laws of quantum physics, specifically the no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance, can guarantee secure communication. Ekert (E91) independently linked security directly to entanglement and to the violation of Bell inequalities, which turned a foundational test of quantum mechanics into a working resource. Together these insights started the field of quantum communication. From them came quantum key distribution networks, satellite links, device-independent cryptography, and quantum teleportation (Bennett and Brassard were co-authors of the 1993 teleportation protocol). Today they underpin worldwide efforts to build a quantum internet. Their work turned quantum non-locality and the impossibility of copying quantum states from paradoxes into technologies. They thereby changed how physicists understand information as a physical quantity. The 2022 prize honoured the experimental tests of entanglement; this prize would recognise the conceptual discoveries that made entanglement and quantum states a resource for communication.
